title: Discovery of a DNA methylation episignature for Weiss-Kruszka syndrome.
authors: McConkey, Haley; van der Laan, Liselot; Ghosh, Sourav; Kleinendorst, Lotte; Levy, Michael A; Rzasa, Jessica; van Hagen, Johanna M; Waisfisz, Quinten; Schulz, Heidi L; Heller, Corina; Huhn, Kerstin; Obermaier, Carolin D; Platzer, Konrad; Jamra, Rami Abou; Marinakis, Nikos; Veltra, Danai; Kosma, Konstantina; Sofocleous, Christalena; Henneman, Peter; Sadikovic, Bekim; van Haelst, Mieke M
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过全基因组DNA甲基化谱发现Weiss-Kruszka综合征的表观签名，虽涉及ZNF462转录因子，但核心是甲基化诊断标志物而非蛋白-DNA互作建模，且无AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WSKA; OMIM 618619) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of ZNF462, a zinc-finger transcription factor involved in chromatin regulation and early embryonic development. WSKA is characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia, craniofacial dysmorphic features (around 8) and variable congenital anomalies. Genome-wide DNAm profiling was performed on peripheral blood DNA from 9 WSKA cases with (likely) pathogenic ZNF462 variants and matched controls to look for differential methylation. Analysis using the EpiSign pipeline identified a robust DNAm pattern, or episignature, specific to WSKA syndrome. Supervised machine-learning classification demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity, with reproducibility confirmed by leave-one-out cross-validation, as well as correctly classifying a validation case with a pathogenic ZNF462 variant. Comparative analysis revealed partial overlap of genome-wide DNA methylation changes between the WSKA episignature and other neurodevelopmental disorders involving chromatin regulators. Functional annotation of differentially methylated probes and regions demonstrated enrichment for pathways related to neurodevelopment, neuron function and cell adhesion. These findings define and validate a distinct DNAm episignature for WSKA, providing a valuable diagnostic biomarker to support variant classification and offering insight into the epigenomic consequences of ZNF462 haploinsufficiency.
abstract_zh: Weiss-Kruszka综合征（WSKA；OMIM 618619）是一种罕见的常染色体显性神经发育障碍，由ZNF462单倍剂量不足引起，ZNF462是一种参与染色质调控和早期胚胎发育的锌指转录因子。WSKA的特征包括发育迟缓、肌张力低下、颅面畸形特征（约8项）及多种先天性异常。对9例携带（可能）致病性ZNF462变异体的WSKA病例及匹配对照组的外周血DNA进行了全基因组DNA甲基化谱分析，以寻找差异甲基化。使用EpiSign流程分析识别出一种稳健的、WSKA综合征特异性的DNA甲基化模式，即表观特征（episignature）。监督式机器学习分类显示出高敏感性和特异性，并通过留一法交叉验证确认了可重复性，同时正确分类了一个携带致病性ZNF462变异体的验证病例。比较分析显示，WSKA表观特征与其他涉及染色质调控因子的神经发育障碍之间的全基因组DNA甲基化变化存在部分重叠。对差异甲基化探针和区域的功能注释表明，与神经发育、神经元功能和细胞粘附相关的通路显著富集。这些发现定义并验证了WSKA独特的DNA甲基化表观特征，为支持变异体分类提供了有价值的诊断生物标志物，并揭示了ZNF462单倍剂量不足的表观基因组后果。
